bib.title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models. Jason Wei, Yi Tay, Rishi Bommasani, Colin Raffel, Barret Zoph, Sebastian Borgeaud, Dani Yogatama, Maarten Bosma, Denny Zhou, Donald Metzler, Ed H. Chi, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Oriol Vinyals, Percy Liang, Jeff Dean, William Fedus. Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 08/2022. arXiv:2206.07682v2 (26 Oct 2022).

COVERAGE: Read all 94,052 of 94,052 chars: body, broader impact, references (skimmed for origins), and Appendices A–F (cross-entropy analysis, alternative metrics, BIG-Bench keyword analysis, MMLU breakdown, model table, parameter-axis plots, task lists). Nothing skipped. This is a survey: it re-plots results from earlier papers. Apart from the Appendix A/B metric and task analyses, it reports no new experiments.

CLAIMS
- claim: The definition. An ability is emergent if smaller models do not have it and larger models do, so you cannot predict it by extrapolating from small models.
  number: none
  setup: a definition applied to pre-trained Transformer LMs
  quote: "An ability is emergent if it is not present in smaller models but is present in larger models."
  where: p2, §2

- claim: Prompting and finetuning techniques count as emergent when they do nothing, or do harm, until the model is large enough.
  number: none
  setup: the criterion for the §4 augmented-prompting strategies
  quote: "If a technique shows no improvement or is harmful when compared to the baseline of not using the technique until applied to a model of a large-enough scale, we also consider the technique an emergent ability."
  where: p4, §4

- claim: Chain-of-thought prompting beats standard prompting on GSM8K only at about 100B parameters. Table 1 lists the threshold as LaMDA 68B.
  number: 10^23 FLOPs (~100B params); Table 1 gives 1.3E+23 / 68B
  setup: LaMDA, GSM8K math word problems, few-shot (Fig 3A, from Wei et al. 2022b)
  quote: "chain of thought prompting only surpasses standard prompting without intermediate steps when scaled to 1023 training FLOPs (∼100B parameters)." Table 1: "Chain-of-thought: Math word problems 1.3E+23 68B LaMDA Wei et al. (2022b)"
  where: p5 §4; Table 1 p6

- claim: Instruction finetuning hurts models of 8B parameters or less and helps only at about 100B. Sanh et al. later got the same behaviour from smaller encoder-decoder T5 models.
  number: hurts at ≤7·10^21 FLOPs (8B); helps at 10^23 (~100B); Table 1 gives 68B, FLAN
  setup: LaMDA/FLAN, average over 10 NLU tasks, zero-shot instructions (Fig 3B, Wei et al. 2022a)
  quote: "this instruction-finetuning technique hurts performance for models of 7 · 1021 training FLOPs (8B parameters) or smaller, and only improves performance when scaled to 1023 training FLOPs (∼100B parameters)"
  where: p5 §4

- claim: A scratchpad (finetuning the model to write out intermediate outputs) helps 8-digit addition only from about 40M parameters up, so its threshold is far lower than CoT's.
  number: ~9·10^19 FLOPs (40M params)
  setup: LaMDA, 8-digit addition, finetuned (Fig 3C, Nye et al. 2021)
  quote: "on 8-digit addition, using a scratchpad only helps for models of ∼9 · 1019 training FLOPs (40M parameters) or larger."
  where: p5 §4

- claim: Self-evaluation calibration ("P(True)") beats standard answer-option calibration only at the largest Anthropic model.
  number: ~3·10^23 FLOPs (52B)
  setup: Anthropic LMs, ECE metric, True/False vs letter choices (Fig 3D, Kadavath et al. 2022)
  quote: "the superiority of the True/False technique only emerges when scaled to the largest model scale of ∼3 · 1023 training FLOPs (52B parameters)."
  where: p5 §4

- claim: Table 1 gives emergence thresholds for other prompting strategies.
  number: self-consistency 68B LaMDA; least-to-most 175B GPT-3; zero-shot CoT 175B GPT-3; CoT StrategyQA 62B PaLM; multilingual CoT 62B PaLM; explanations in prompt 280B Gopher; ask-me-anything 6B EleutherAI
  setup: each threshold is taken from the cited paper's model family
  quote: "Self-consistency decoding 1.3E+23 68B LaMDA Wang et al. (2022b)"; "Least-to-most prompting 3.1E+23 175B GPT-3 Zhou et al. (2022)"; "Zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning 3.1E+23 175B GPT-3 Kojima et al. (2022)"; "Leveraging explanations in prompting 5.0E+23 280B Gopher Lampinen et al. (2022)"; "Ask me anything prompting 1.4E+22 6B EleutherAI Arora et al. (2022)"
  where: Table 1, p6

- claim: Few-shot arithmetic jumps from near zero to well above random at 13B for GPT-3 and 68B for LaMDA.
  number: 2·10^22 FLOPs (13B) GPT-3; 10^23 (68B) LaMDA
  setup: BIG-Bench modified arithmetic, 2-shot
  quote: "before performance jumps to sharply above random at 2 · 1022 training FLOPs (13B parameters) for GPT-3, and 1023 training FLOPs (68B parameters) for LaMDA."
  where: p3 §3

- claim: On MMLU, models of about 10B parameters or less score no better than guessing. Models of 70B–280B score well above random.
  number: ~10^22 FLOPs (~10B) vs 3–5·10^23 (70B–280B)
  setup: GPT-3, Gopher, Chinchilla, few-shot, average over 57 topics
  quote: "models of ∼1022 training FLOPs (∼10B parameters) or smaller do not perform better than guessing on average over all the topics, scaling up to 3–5 ·1023 training FLOPs (70B–280B parameters) enables performance to substantially surpass random."
  where: p3 §3

- claim: WiC stayed at random through GPT-3 175B and Chinchilla. It rose above random only at PaLM 540B, with no architecture change. This contradicts Brown et al.'s guess that the cause was architecture.
  number: 2.5·10^24 FLOPs (540B)
  setup: Word in Context, one-shot
  quote: "above-random performance eventually emerged when PaLM was scaled to 2.5 · 1024 FLOPs (540B parameters)"
  where: p4 §3; p6–7 §5

- claim: The threshold depends on more than scale. On 14 BIG-Bench tasks, PaLM 62B is above random while LaMDA 137B and GPT-3 175B are near random. The paper suggests data quality and architecture as reasons.
  number: 14 tasks
  setup: BIG-Bench; task list in Appendix F
  quote: "there are 14 BIG-Bench tasks5 for which LaMDA 137B and GPT-3 175B models perform at near-random, but PaLM 62B in fact achieves above-random performance, despite having fewer model parameters and training FLOPs."
  where: p7 §5.2

- claim: Later methods brought emergent abilities to smaller models: instruction following in an 11B encoder-decoder (T0), and RLHF that let a 1.3B InstructGPT beat much larger models in human ratings.
  number: 11B; 1.3B
  setup: Sanh et al. 2022; Ouyang et al. 2022
  quote: "Ouyang et al. (2022) proposed a finetuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback approach for the InstructGPT models, which enabled a 1.3B model to outperform much larger models in human-rater evaluations"
  where: p8 §5.2

- claim: Metric choice. Cross-entropy loss keeps improving while exact match, BLEU or accuracy sits at random, so the downstream metric hides gradual gains. All six LaMDA emergent tasks show this (Outcome 2). The authors still say this does not explain emergence or predict where it happens.
  number: six tasks; flat region ≤10^22 FLOPs / ≤27B
  setup: LaMDA, six BIG-Bench tasks (Figs 5–6)
  quote: "cross-entropy loss improves even for small model scales where the downstream metrics (exact match, BLEU, and accuracy) are close to random and do not improve, which shows that improvements in the log-likelihood of the target sequence can be masked by such downstream metrics. However, this analysis does not explain why downstream metrics are emergent"
  where: p7 §5.1; App A.1 p19

- claim: Metrics that give partial credit (BLEU, ROUGE, BLEURT) show the same jump on generative tasks, so the authors argue exact match is not a complete explanation. The jump also appears on classification tasks.
  number: none
  setup: modified arithmetic, IPA transliterate, periodic elements (Fig 7)
  quote: "we conclude that using exact string match instead of another evaluation metric that awards partial credit is not a complete explanation of emergence on generative tasks."
  where: App A.2 p22

- claim: Prompting best practice is expected to change as models get stronger.
  number: none
  setup: discussion
  quote: "it is also likely that the best practices for prompting will change as more-powerful models are developed over time."
  where: p11 §5.6

- claim: A hand count of BIG-Bench tasks found no clear pattern in which task types are emergent. Arithmetic and mathematics had a surprisingly low share of emergent tasks.
  number: 210 tasks classified; visual reasoning flat in 8/13
  setup: two co-authors labelled the tasks by agreement
  quote: "Overall, there are no clear trends for which types of tasks are most emergent."
  where: App A.3 p23

- claim: Some risks grow with scale. Larger models memorise more training data. GPT-3 imitated human falsehoods more as it grew. Bias on ambiguous BBQ contexts can rise with scale.
  number: none
  setup: survey of prior work
  quote: "larger models were found to be more likely to memorize training data (Carlini et al., 2021; 2022)"
  where: p9 §5.4

LIMITS
- It is a survey of other papers' results. Thresholds come from different model families, prompts and papers, and the paper does not run controlled comparisons.
- The authors say the threshold is not a fixed property of the ability: "Our goal in this paper is not to characterize or claim that a specific scale is required to observe emergent abilities" (p3). Better data, architecture or training can lower it (§5.2).
- Scale variables are correlated. Training data size is not plotted because many model families train every size on the same number of tokens. Chinchilla and MoE models break the link between parameters and FLOPs.
- Labelling a task "emergent" is subjective: it depends on what counts as "near-random" (App A.3).
- On metrics, they concede that exact-match scoring "may disguise compounding incremental improvements as emergence". They argue it is "at best an incomplete explanation". Their own cross-entropy analysis shows gradual underlying improvement but does not predict where the jump happens.
- Dated: these are 2022 models (LaMDA, GPT-3, PaLM). The ~100B CoT and instruction-tuning thresholds have since dropped a long way, which the authors anticipate in §5.2. The paper does not address the later "emergence is a mirage of the metric" critique; that critique postdates it. Do not present the thresholds as current.

BUILDS ON: Anderson 1972 ("More Is Different"); Steinhardt 2022 (definition adapted); Huberman & Hogg 1987 (phase transitions); Kaplan et al. 2020 and Hoffmann et al. 2022 (scaling laws); Brown et al. 2020 (few-shot prompting); BIG-Bench 2022; Ganguli et al. 2022 (predictability and surprise). For the §4 strategies: Wei et al. 2022b (CoT), Wei et al. 2022a (FLAN), Nye et al. 2021 (scratchpad), Kadavath et al. 2022 (P(True)), Wang et al. 2022b (self-consistency), Kojima et al. 2022 (zero-shot CoT), Zhou et al. 2022 (least-to-most), Lampinen et al. 2022 (explanations), Sanh et al. 2022 (T0), Ouyang et al. 2022 (InstructGPT).

CODE: none in the source.

FIGURES
- Figure 3, p5: four panels (CoT on GSM8K, instruction tuning, scratchpad, calibration), each showing technique vs no technique against training FLOPs, LaMDA (A–C) and Anthropic (D). The single best figure for 03-core-techniques: it shows where the CoT and no-CoT curves cross, and instruction tuning underperforming below 8B. Figure 12 (p28) is the same with parameters on the x-axis, which is easier for learners to read.
- Table 1, p6: a list of emergence thresholds by ability and prompting strategy. Compact as a reference slide, with a "2022 models" caveat.
- Figure 2, p4: eight few-shot tasks with the flat-then-jump shape. Shows what "emergence" looks like.
- Figure 5, p20: error rate and cross-entropy side by side. Shows quickly that loss improves while the metric stays flat (the metric-choice point).
- Figure 7, p22: emergence persists across EM, BLEU, ROUGE and BLEURT.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean. Exponents lose their superscript ("1023" means 10^23; "2 · 1022" means 2·10^22). Quotes above keep the raw extracted text.
- Internal inconsistencies to watch when citing:
  - The prose gives the CoT and instruction-tuning thresholds as "∼100B parameters". Table 1 gives 68B. Table 2 lists the LaMDA size as 69B.
  - Calibration: the prose says ∼3·10^23 FLOPs for 52B and Table 1 says 2.6E+23, but Table 2 lists Anthropic 52B at "2.65E+22". That is probably a typo in Table 2.
  - Table 2 prints "Chinchilla ... 7.1B [sic]".
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
